title: The Toddy Drinker's Cirrhosis, Surfacing After His Wife's Death

sections.heading: The Patient's Story
sections.content:
He is 50 years old. Seven months before this admission, he developed low-grade fever with yellowing of his eyes, followed by gradually worsening pitting edema in both legs. Abdominal distension followed, along with decreased urine output. He was managed conservatively at a local hospital and his symptoms eased, but he kept having on-and-off recurrences. In November, three months before this admission, he was diagnosed with hepatitis B surface antigen positivity — though no ascitic fluid tap was ever attempted at that time. A report from that period showed his platelet count at 65,000 and hemoglobin at 11.2%.

He has been drinking alcohol since age 20, typically 90 mL daily plus an occasional glass of a local liquor (saara). Three years ago, his wife died, and his alcohol intake climbed — from a quarter to a half bottle — along with an increase in toddy. He notices his symptoms worsen with non-vegetarian food and toddy, and ease with a vegetarian diet and medication.

sections.heading: What the Work-Up Showed So Far
sections.content:
- General exam: conscious, coherent, cooperative, moderately built; no icterus, cyanosis, clubbing, or lymphadenopathy
- Vitals: blood pressure 110/70 mmHg, pulse 87 bpm, respiratory rate 22/min, oxygen saturation 98% on room air
- Abdominal exam: distended abdomen with a partially everted central umbilicus, striae above the umbilicus, engorged abdominal veins, dullness on percussion over the epigastrium and flanks, shifting dullness and a fluid thrill present, consistent with ascites; soft and non-tender on palpation with no organomegaly; bowel sounds present
- Cardiorespiratory exam: unremarkable
- Neurological exam: normal
- Investigations sent: blood counts, liver and renal function panels, and further imaging and fluid studies (documented but not detailed in the available record)

Working diagnosis: known hepatitis B surface antigen positivity with cirrhosis.

sections.heading: How the Story Unfolded on the Ward
sections.content: He was started on spironolactone and furosemide for his ascites. His regimen remained unchanged through the following day, and on the second day of this documented course, an injection of vitamin K was added — a step consistent with addressing an underlying coagulopathy from his liver disease. His case illustrates a slow-burning presentation: hepatitis B surface antigen positivity uncovered incidentally months earlier, alcohol use that intensified after a personal loss, and a cirrhosis picture that had been building quietly before finally bringing him in with decompensated ascites.
